policy.scope: canonical semantic checking, checked names/types/ownership/effects/state facts, and registered rejection diagnostics
policy.foreign_suffix: lowering, optimization, prelude, runtime, and foreign tools remain explicit downstream boundaries

claim.statement: For an identified UTF-8 Jet source, the canonical compiler checking route emits the checked semantic index and registered diagnostics through one production front end; finite observations remain bounded evidence rather than universal proof.
preconditions: The compiler check operation is the production jet inspect compiler check seam, not a second parser or checker.
The entry source bytes and all implementation authorities are identified by SHA-256.
Names, types, ownership, effects, state, and fact records are interpreted through the canonical sema and Facts implementations.
A rejection has a registered diagnostic code, explanation, fix, and source span.
A tool crash, timeout, signal, unavailable binary, or malformed response is not an ordinary checking rejection.
unsupported_cases: A missing, stale, or unbound checking witness
A compiler response without the versioned CompilerChecked value
A semantic index with a source digest different from the checked source
A rejection without a registered diagnostic code, reason, fix, or valid span
An unavailable compiler, tool crash, timeout, or malformed JSON response
A changed sema, Facts, Core authority, compiler inspection seam, or implementation input

execution.command: scripts/agent/jet-env full jet inspect compiler check <entry>
execution.crash_policy: tool failures are unavailable or invalid_oracle, never checking rejection

binding_methods.implementation: the canonical sema, Facts registry, semantic-index builder, compiler inspection seam, and loader
binding_methods.construction: the versioned CompilerChecked value with exact source digest, semantic index, facts, spans, and diagnostics
binding_methods.limit: finite checking witnesses do not establish universal preservation

binding_methods.candidate_binding: recorded implementation paths and compiler-proof identity
binding_methods.limit: the checker observes the production seam; it is not a mechanized theorem about every sema state

binding_methods.certificate: retained accepted, rejected, alias, ownership, effect, state, fact, derivation, and forged-record controls
binding_methods.limit: observed certificates and negative controls are finite and remain proof-blocking

obligations.subject: types, generics, overloads, conversions, and exhaustiveness

coverage.qualification_rule: Every checking boundary row stays blocked unless its implementation correspondence, current identity, binding, and bounded witness disposition are all explicit; no finite corpus claims universal proof.

facts.canonical_rule: FactRegistry and DerivationRecord are the only fact/derivation authorities; this checker consumes their projections and does not define a parallel fact model.

core.authority_rule: Core inventory and ledger entries remain canonical inputs; checking does not create a second Core table or denominator.

proven: The checker validates the checking contract, witness schema, compiler identity, implementation binding, and obligation ownership.
The production compiler check seam is compared with exact source bytes, semantic-index facts, source spans, and registered diagnostics.
Tool failures, stale identities, malformed responses, forged facts, and missing boundaries cannot qualify as checking proof.
assumed: The ratified sema, Facts, Core ledger, and architecture sources state the intended checking law.
The compiler inspection command reaches the same loader, parser, sema, fact, and diagnostic paths used by ordinary compilation.
The pinned jet.compiler-proof.v1 claim identifies the selected candidate toolchain.
tested: Accepted witnesses retain names, typed signatures, ownership/view metadata, effect provenance, state/fact records, and derivations.
Rejected witnesses retain registered diagnostics with reasons, fixes, and source spans.
Forged type, ownership, effect, state, fact, alias, and derivation records are rejected by the checker.
blocked: Universal preservation for every semantic input and every compiler state.
A fresh compiler replay or complete witness qualification when the pinned compiler is unavailable.
Lowering, optimization, Prelude, runtime, adapter, and foreign-tool preservation beyond this checking boundary.
